data.narrative:
The Exploration Company is a Series B–stage space and aerospace firm that has raised $160M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 5 private companies at Series B/C stages (Sierra Space at $8.0B, Cowboy Space Corporation at $2.0B, Varda Space Industries at $1.5B, Aalyria at $1.3B, and Skyryse at $1.1B) and 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL).

Two methods triangulate valuation. Stage-progression applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, deriving $304M from the $160M capital base. Peer-median analysis across the five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies yields $1.5B, reflecting the middle of the $1.1B–$8.0B range. Public-comp anchoring, while structurally applicable to the Space & Aerospace sector (which trades at a 23.9x median price-to-sales across 6 tickers), cannot be applied here due to absence of target revenue data—typical for private companies.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $258M (low) to $1.7B (high), with a median of $902M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around The Exploration Company's revenue trajectory, market position within a heterogeneous peer set, and stage-specific risk factors. The peer-median method carries higher conviction given direct comparability, though the $8.0B outlier (Sierra Space) illustrates significant valuation dispersion in early-stage aerospace.
